caveat: Published official website roster; source is legacy content and does not establish current appointments. No subject specializations are published. BSDMIA and BLIS associations below are coordinator roles, not invented teaching assignments.

institution.visionParaphrase: Academic excellence in information technology education that responds to the needs of the whole person and the wider world.
institution.missionParaphrase: Educate students through Christian principles and computer studies practice, preparing them for further study, computing careers, information management, and lifelong learning.
institution.qualityParaphrase: Combine Christian values, academic excellence, professionalism, and continuous improvement in service to the university and its partners.

timeline.text: The BSCS program began under the College of Commerce, with about 100 students.
The College of Computer Studies opened in Mary Thomas Building, led by its first dean, Engr. Cirilo C. Calibjo.
The college introduced Digital Media and Interactive Arts.
Library and Information Science joined the college.

BSIT.summary: Prepare to plan, integrate, operate, and maintain computing technologies for organizations and their users.
objectives: Analyze user needs and select suitable technology
Practice ethical teamwork and lifelong learning
BSIT.curriculumNote: Published curriculum is labeled effective AY 2018–2019; describe topic highlights rather than imply a current official course checklist.

BSCS.summary: Study computing theory, algorithms, and software development to solve complex problems.
objectives: Communicate and work responsibly in diverse teams
BSCS.careerNote: Software developer, software engineer, and computing research are plausible career pathways inferred from the published curriculum; label as pathways rather than official placement promises.

BSDMIA.summary: Combine creative practice, applied arts, and technology to produce digital experiences for entertainment, education, and communication.
objectives: Connect traditional arts with digital media
Develop and evaluate creative solutions for user needs

BLIS.summary: A four-year program preparing students to develop and manage print, multimedia, electronic, and digital information resources.
objectives: Select, organize, and share information resources
Assess user needs and improve information services
BLIS.careerNote: Librarian and information services professional are pathways supported by the program description; no licensure guarantee.
BLIS.sourceWarning: Source contains obvious copied labels (BSIS graduate heading and Computer Science Society text). Do not reproduce these errors. Use LIS-coded outcomes and BLIS description.
